enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **g)** The job I will like to do when I grow up.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: name the job (a medical doctor) and say why it is noble.
2. The origin of the ambition: the narrator's sick brother and the village doctor.
3. The studies and the hard work needed.
4. What the narrator will do after qualifying (health centre in the village).
5. Benefits and difficulties of the job, conclusion.

**Model composition (461 words)**

When I grow up, I would like to become a medical doctor. This ambition was born during my childhood, and it has grown stronger with every year. I believe that no job is more noble than saving human lives, and I want to serve my community in this way.

My desire began when I was eight. My younger brother fell seriously ill with malaria, and our village had no doctor. My mother carried him for hours on her back to the nearest health centre, and I walked behind them, crying. A kind doctor treated him, and within days he was playing again. I looked at that doctor in his white coat and decided that I wanted to be like him.

To become a doctor, I know that I must work very hard. I must pass my GCE examinations with excellent grades in Biology, Chemistry and Physics, and then enter the Faculty of Medicine, where I will study for at least seven years. I will also practise in a hospital under experienced doctors before I treat patients alone. I will also read widely, ask questions in class and join the science club of my school, so that I prepare myself early. I am ready for all this sacrifice, because I do not fear hard work.

Once I qualify, I will return to my village and open a health centre. Many people in rural areas die from simple diseases, because they cannot afford the cost of transport to the town. In my health centre, I will treat the poor at a low price, give advice on hygiene and organise vaccination campaigns for children. I will also train young people as nurses, so that the centre will continue to serve the people after me.

Apart from the satisfaction of helping others, the job of a doctor brings other benefits. A doctor is respected by everybody in society and earns a good salary, which allows him to take care of his own family. He also continues to learn new things throughout his life, because medicine is always changing.

However, I know the job is not easy. A doctor works long hours, sometimes at night, and must stay calm when a patient is in pain or dies. He has to put the needs of others before his own comfort. But this does not discourage me, because these difficulties also give the job its value.

In conclusion, I dream of becoming a doctor who loves his patients and serves the poor. I pray that God will give me health, strength and wisdom to reach my goal, and I promise to work hard every day until the dream comes true. I also hope to inspire other children from my village to study hard and follow the same path.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Naming a job but giving no reasons, steps or personal experience: the composition must explain WHY and HOW.
2. Writing about several jobs at once instead of one clear choice, or ending without a conclusion.
